question.text: A 35-year-old earns Rs.15,00,000 per year and plans to retire at 60. If income grows at 8% annually, what will the gross income be at retirement?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook future-income formula is Current value x (1 + growth rate)^(years to retirement). Here: Rs.15,00,000 x (1.08)^25, which equals approximately Rs.1,02,72,713. The Trap: Applying simple interest (Rs.15,00,000 + Rs.15,00,000 x 8% x 25 = Rs.45,00,000) ignores compounding and yields a substantially understated figure. Note: Always use compound growth for future-income projections; this is the first step of the Income Replacement Method.
